chapterNote: A psalm in two halves that do not seem to belong together until the last verses join them. The first four verses are an anatomy of the wicked man, told from the inside. Transgression itself delivers an oracle in his heart — there is no dread of God before his eyes — and from that one missing fear everything else follows. He flatters himself until he cannot see his own guilt; his mouth produces trouble and deceit; he has stopped being wise; he plots on his bed, takes his stand on a bad road, and no longer even rejects evil. Paul closes Romans 3's indictment of the whole human race with the first verse. Then, without transition, the sky opens: Your covenant love is in the heavens, Your faithfulness reaches the clouds, Your righteousness is like the mountains of God, Your judgments a vast deep — and You keep man and beast alive. The children of men shelter under Your wings, feast on the rich fare of Your house, drink from the river of Your delights. With You is the fountain of life, and in Your light we see light — the verse the church has used for the doctrine that God is known only by His own illumination. The prayer at the end asks for that love to keep coming and for the foot of pride to be kept off — and the last verse shows the wicked man, fallen where he stood.

1.text: Transgression speaks its oracle to the wicked man — I hear it deep in my heart: there is no dread of God before his eyes.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm of David the servant [ebed] of the LORD [YHWH]. The transgression [pesha] of the wicked [rasha] says [neum — utters an oracle] within [qereb] my heart [leb], that there is no fear [pachad — dread] of God [Elohim] before his eyes [ayin].
1.notes: neum-pesha la-rasha be-qereb libbi (H5002, H6588, H7563, H7130, H3820): neum is the prophet's oracle-word — the 'saith the LORD' that seals a prophecy — and here Transgression is the one delivering it, deep inside the wicked man. The Masoretic Text, followed by the KJV, reads 'my heart' — David overhearing the oracle; the Greek and Syriac versions and a few Hebrew manuscripts read libbo, 'his heart'. Its content: en-pachad Elohim le-neged enav (H6343, H430, H5869) — no dread of God in his field of view (cf. Romans 3:18, Paul's closing charge in his indictment of the race).

2.text: For he flatters himself in his own eyes, so that his iniquity is never found out and hated.
2.amp: For he flatters [chalaq — smooths] himself in his own eyes [ayin], until his iniquity [avon] be found ['to find his iniquity to hate', matsa, the KJV margin] to be hateful [sane].
2.notes: hecheliq elav be-enav (H2505, H5869): he has smoothed things over toward himself — the flattery-verb of Psalm 5:9, turned inward — li-mtso avono li-sno (H4672, H5771, H8130): so as to find his guilt and hate it — which, the margin's literal reading shows, he never does. Self-flattery is the mechanism that keeps sin from being noticed.

3.text: The words of his mouth are trouble and deceit; he has stopped acting wisely, stopped doing good.
3.amp: The words [dabar] of his mouth [peh] are iniquity [aven] and deceit [mirmah]: he has left off [chadal — ceased] to be wise [sakal] and to do good [yatab].
3.notes: dibre-phiv aven u-mirmah (H1697, H6310, H205, H4820): the output of the flattered self is aven, trouble, and mirmah, fraud. chadal le-haskil le-hetib (H2308, H7919, H3190): he STOPPED — chadal pictures a man who has given up even the outward prudence and decency he once kept up.

4.text: He plots trouble on his bed; he stations himself on a road that is not good; he does not reject evil.
4.amp: He devises [chashab — schemes] mischief ['vanity', aven, the KJV margin] upon his bed [mishkab]; he sets [yatsab — takes his stand] himself in a way [derek] that is not good [tov]; he abhors [maas — rejects] not evil [ra].
4.notes: aven yachshov al-mishkabo (H205, H2803, H4904): the bed that Psalm 4:4 made a place of examination is here a planning room. yityatsseb al-derekh lo-tov (H3320, H1870, H2896): he takes his STAND on a bad road — commitment, not drift. ra lo yimas (H7451, H3988): and the final symptom, the loss of the reflex to reject evil.

5.text: O LORD, Your covenant love is in the heavens; Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
5.amp: Your mercy [chesed — covenant love], O LORD [YHWH], is in the heavens [shamayim]; and Your faithfulness [emunah] reaches unto the clouds [shechaqim].
5.notes: The psalm turns from the wicked man's ceiling — his own eyes — to God's: YHWH be-ha-shamayim chasdekha (H8064, H2617), emunatekha ad-shechaqim (H530, H7834). Psalm 57:10's vertical measurement: covenant love and faithfulness taller than the sky.

6.text: Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; Your judgments are a vast deep. O LORD, You preserve man and beast alike.
6.amp: Your righteousness [tsedaqah] is like the great ['the mountains of God', El, the KJV margin] mountains [har]; Your judgments [mishpat] are a great [rav] deep [tehom — abyss]: O LORD [YHWH], You preserve [yasha — save] man [adam] and beast [behemah].
6.notes: tsidqatekha ke-harere-El (H6666, H2042, H410): the margin's literal — righteousness like the mountains OF GOD, mountains too big to belong to anyone else — mishpatekha tehom rabbah (H4941, H8415, H7227): judgments like the primeval deep, the tehom of Genesis 1:2, too deep to see the bottom. adam u-behemah toshia YHWH (H120, H929, H3467): and the same God keeps the cattle alive (cf. Jonah 4:11).

7.text: How precious is Your covenant love, O God! The children of men take refuge under the shadow of Your wings.
7.amp: How excellent ['precious', yaqar, the KJV margin] is Your lovingkindness [chesed — covenant love], O God [Elohim]! therefore the children [ben] of men [adam] put their trust [chasah — take refuge] under the shadow [tsel] of Your wings [kanaph].
7.notes: mah-yaqar chasdekha Elohim (H3368, H2617, H430): precious — the yaqar of Psalm 116:15, value by weight. u-bene adam be-tsel kenaphekha yechesayun (H1121, H120, H6738, H3671, H2620): the sons of Adam — humanity in general, not Israel only — sheltering under the wings: the cherubim's wings over the mercy seat, and Jesus' hen over Jerusalem (cf. Matthew 23:37).

8.text: They drink their fill of the rich fare of Your house, and You give them to drink from the river of Your delights.
8.amp: They shall be abundantly satisfied ['watered', ravah — drenched, the KJV margin] with the fatness [deshen — richness] of Your house [bayith]; and You shall make them drink [shaqah] of the river [nachal] of Your pleasures [eden — delights].
8.notes: yirveyun mi-deshen betekha (H7301, H1880, H1004): drenched — the margin's 'watered' — with the fat of Your house, the sacrificial feast. ve-nachal adanekha tashqem (H5158, H5730, H8248): the river of Your delights — adanim, the plural of eden, 'delight', written with the very letters of the garden's name; the echo of Eden is hard to miss, and God's house has the garden's river running through it (cf. Genesis 2:10; Revelation 22:1).

9.text: For the fountain of life is with You; in Your light we see light.
9.amp: For with You is the fountain [maqor — source, spring] of life [chay]: in Your light [or] shall we see [raah] light [or].
9.notes: ki-immekha meqor chayyim (H4726, H2416): the SOURCE of life is with You — Jeremiah 2:13's 'fountain of living waters'. be-orekha nireh-or (H216, H7200): in Your light we see light — the sentence Augustine and Calvin both used for the doctrine that God is known only by God's own illumination; John 1:4's 'in Him was life, and the life was the light of men'.

10.text: Draw out Your covenant love toward those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.
10.amp: O continue ['draw out at length', mashak, the KJV margin] Your lovingkindness [chesed — covenant love] unto them that know [yada] You; and Your righteousness [tsedaqah] to the upright [yashar] in heart [leb].
10.notes: meshokh chasdekha le-yodeekha (H4900, H2617, H3045): mashak is 'draw, drag, prolong' — the margin's 'draw out at length': keep the covenant love coming, to those who KNOW You — ve-tsidqatekha le-yishre-leb (H6666, H3477, H3820). The petition after nine verses of description.

11.text: Do not let the foot of pride come marching over me, or the hand of the wicked drive me out.
11.amp: Let not the foot [regel] of pride [gaavah] come [bo] against me, and let not the hand [yad] of the wicked [rasha] remove [nud — shake me off, drive me to wander] me.
11.notes: al-tevoeni regel gaavah (H935, H7272, H1346): the FOOT of pride — arrogance pictured as a boot coming down — ve-yad-reshaim al-tenideni (H3027, H7563, H5110): nud is 'to wander, be shaken'; the wicked's hand trying to shake David loose from his place. The wicked man of verses 1-4 is now at the door.

12.text: There they lie — the workers of iniquity, fallen; thrown down, and unable to rise.
12.amp: There are the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven] fallen [naphal]: they are cast down [dachah — thrust down], and shall not be able [yakol] to rise [qum].
12.notes: sham naphelu poale aven (H5307, H6466, H205): THERE — the psalmist points, as if at the spot — the evildoers have fallen; dochu ve-lo-yakhelu qum (H1760, H3201, H6965): shoved down, unable to get up. The oracle of verse 1 has its answer: the man with no dread of God ends on the ground.
